identified_issues: Proxy-observation conflation: The automated monitoring system conflated transport-layer response codes (HTTP 504 GATEWAY_TIMEOUT) with authoritative underlying settlement state (S != O != E).

Premature ledger rollback hazard: Issuing a rollback on SETTLE_BATCH_8102 based solely on gateway submission timeout would introduce an unhedged 14.85M EUR balance discrepancy against the central clearing network.
Single-channel epistemic failure: Downstream operations monitoring failed to synthesize the authoritative out-of-band CAMT.053/MT940 settlement feed before asserting transaction failure.
evidence: Clearing Bank SFTP Bilateral Statement (CAMT.053 / MT940 End-of-Window Feed at 08:30:00Z) explicitly records finalized entry REF=TX-8102-EUR with CLEARING_ID=EBA-STEP2-9948102, AMT=14850000.00 EUR, STATUS=SETTLED, and VAL_DATETIME=2026-10-06T08:15:02Z.
Clearing bank statement reports 'REJECTION_RECORDS: NONE', confirming that no RJCT or PACR negative return records exist for this instruction.
Core Financial Ledger Engine (LEDGER_CORE_01) correctly committed TX-8102-EUR at 2026-10-06T08:15:00.120Z for EUR 14,850,000.00 prior to clearing finalization.
The HTTP 504 GATEWAY_TIMEOUT recorded at 2026-10-06T08:15:03.205Z was a transport timeout occurring after the settlement had already been finalized at 2026-10-06T08:15:02Z on the clearing endpoint.
recommended_action: Reject the automated alert's rollback directive and preserve the committed ledger state. Update the operations monitor to enforce the Separation Axiom (S != O != E), forbidding ledger mutation or definitive settlement failure rulings on gateway timeouts until reconciled against out-of-band CAMT.053/MT940 clearing statements.
